question.name: Question 8
question.worked_solution:
First, we simplify the limit:

$$
{lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\frac{9}{12{x}^{4}}={lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\frac{3}{4{x}^{4}}
$$

Then, we use the algebra of limits to pull out the constant factor of $\frac{3}{4}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\frac{3}{4{x}^{4}} & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\frac{3}{4}\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{4}} \\  & =\frac{3}{4}\cdot {lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\frac{1}{{x}^{4}}\end{aligned}
$$

We recall the graph of the function $y=\frac{1}{{x}^{4}}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14247879/assets/fa92c457186fbdf71552ec79c782af7983e6fa09009e7f0efdd02b8f74e3ab98.png)

From the graph, we see that

$$
{lim}_{x\to ({0}^{+})}\frac{1}{{x}^{4}}=\infty 
$$

The positive factor of $\frac{3}{4}$ does not change the sign of the limit. Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{3}{4}\cdot {lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}\frac{1}{{x}^{4}}=\infty .
$$
